address: 2155–2159 Golden Gate Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94118
hook: First A.M.E. Zion Church, built in 1960 to Robert Batchelor's design after redevelopment took the congregation's Geary Street home.

parcel.note: The church stands on two parcels, 1160029 and 1160030, which the Board of Supervisors named together in its 2026 landmark initiation. Both carry the same 2155–2159 address range and the same recorded lot area (3,436 sq ft) and land value ($36,705); only 1160030 carries a building area (9,800 sq ft) and an improvement value. The figures on this page are the two rows as the roll states them, not a reconciliation of them. The assessor files the parcels under North Panhandle; the city's analysis-neighborhood layer places them in Lone Mountain/USF, which this site follows.

assessment.note: Land value is the figure recorded identically on each of the two parcels; the improvement value is the one recorded on 1160030. Lot 1160029 carries no improvement value at all.

permits.description: Steel steeple installed in place of the original wood one, to match it.

permit_summary.note: DBI files one permit under 2155 Golden Gate Avenue and the other under 2159.

historical_record.description: The Board of Supervisors initiated Article 10 landmark designation of the First AME Zion Church at 2155–2159 Golden Gate Avenue, citing the congregation's history and the building as an example of mid-century modern architecture, and asked the Planning Department to prepare a designation report. File No. 260259.
The congregation moved into a new building on this site, designed by architect Robert Batchelor.
The congregation's previous home at 1669 Geary Street in the Western Addition was demolished for redevelopment.
The congregation moved into a classic structure on Stockton Street between Clay and Sacramento, bought from a Unitarian congregation.
The Reverend John Jamison Moore founded the church, then the AME Zion Church, on Stockton Street between Broadway and Vallejo. The building no longer stands.

narrative.lead: The church stands on two parcels, block 1160 lots 029 and 030, which the Board of Supervisors named together when it initiated landmark designation.

unknowns: Whether the Historic Preservation Commission has recommended landmark designation since the Board initiated it in March 2026.
How the two parcels divide the building, and why the roll records the same lot area and land value on each.
The date of the last recorded sale.
